facts.text: Nezu Shrine was founded in the 1st century by Yamato Takeru, son of Emperor Keikō, per legend.
The shrine was relocated to Nezu in 1705 by Tokugawa Tsunayoshi, the fifth shōgun, and later chosen as guardian deity by his successor Tokugawa Ienobu.
Nezu Shrine’s main building is built in Ishi-no-ma-zukuri style, modeled after Nikkō Tōshō-gū, and several structures are designated Important Cultural Property.
The shrine hosts an Azalea Festival from early April to early May, drawing visitors to its blooming azaleas and earning the nickname “Tokyo’s most beautiful shrine.”.
Nezu Shrine sits beside a pond of koi, with a viewing platform midway along the path that offers a view of the main precincts.
